title: Episodic prober for hybrid-kernel occupancy and latency regulator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Build an "episodic prober" subsystem that runs short, controlled micro-workloads (episodes) to measure real-time kernel occupancy, per-kernel latency, and GPU utilization across architecture families and sequence-length buckets. Use these episodic signals to drive an online latency regulator that selects kernel variants (fast-path, high-occupancy, quantized) for each incoming request profile. Goals: (1) reduce tail latency regressions from suboptimal kernel picks during workload shifts, (2) improve average GPU occupancy and throughput for mixed seqlen workloads, (3) limit online probing cost and avoid unstable thrashing between kernels. Constraints: episodes must be lightweight (<= 5% extra token cost on sampled machines), must be safe for production (no user-visible correctness changes), must respect SLOs and dedicated capacity isolation. Architecture notes: - Episodic sampling controller schedules short probe episodes at low-priority times or on controlled worker pool. Episodes vary sequence length, batch shapes, and prefill/decode ratio to generate fingerprints. - Fingerprint store: compact per-worker histogram of measured latencies, occupancy, and KV cache hit characteristics keyed by (arch, seqlen_bucket, model_variant). Warm-start lookup uses offline cost model to seed priors. - Latency regulator: a policy layer that combines episodic empirical signals with the cost model to compute a per-request kernel score; policy supports hard SLO constraints (e.g., 95p latency cap) and soft cost objectives (batching/occupancy improvements). - Exploration schedule: bandit-inspired episodic exploration with decreasing exploration rates, and episodic rollback if a probe causes SLO violation. - Integration with prefill/decode scheduler: regulator influences prefilling kernel choice and decode kernel choice, and signals the scheduler to co-schedule compatible requests to preserve batching / KV locality. Implementation plan: - Phase 1: standalone episodic prober binary and telemetry pipeline, synthetic episodes for typical seqlen buckets. - Phase 2: integrate fingerprint store and regulator into routing layer; add canary toggle that routes 1% traffic through regulator decisions. - Phase 3: closed-loop rollout with automatic rollback heuristics on SLO regressions, and admin tuning UI in Console for exploration budget. Acceptance criteria: - No more than 3% regression in 95p latency during canary vs baseline; roll out blocked if >5% regression. - Demonstrated throughput uplift (tokens/sec) >= 6% on mixed seqlen benchmark and cost per token <= 10% reduction in steady-state. - Probe cost overhead <= 5% of total tokens on probed machines. - Audit logs for all kernel switches and probe episodes. Rollout/Risks: Start in hosted dev pool, then Dedicated non-production clusters, then private beta. Risk: noisy probes interfering with SLOs; mitigations include strict isolation, probe throttling, and immediate rollback triggers. Operational metrics: 95p latency, median latency, tokens/sec, probe_rate, kernel_switch_rate, probe_cost_pct. Related: references internal design doc and offline cost model.
